title: 62. The Evolution of the Treatment Industry, Navigating Adolescent Addiction, and the Compassionate Care Model feat. Evan Haines
description_html:
Today I am joined by Evan Haines. Evan is the co-founder of Alo House, a leader in the compassionate care model, and an active member in the recovery community. He works to connect with individuals and help them obtain and maintain sobriety through compassion rather than control. (bio adapted from alorecovery.com)

Evan’s Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/itsevanhaines/?hl=en

Alo House (offering Detox, Inpatient & Outpatient and dual-diagnosis treatment): https://alorecovery.com/
talk_about: Evan's journey to sobriety and working in the addiction treatment industry
How mental health and addiction treatment has evolved over the last few centuries
How addiction and mental health challenges are the result of an environment, emotional sensitivity, and relationships
The direction we as a society to increase connection, compassion, and decrease the mental health challenges plaguing America
mentioned_html:
+ Alo House

+ Alcoholics Anonymous

+ Lost Connections by Johann Hari

+ Andrea Arlington (Life Coach specializing in Family Recovery)
guests: evan haines, co-founder of alo house
summary: sadie talks with evan haines, co-founder of alo house, about his journey to sobriety after his mother's suicide when he was 14, his drunk driving arrest at 30, and finding recovery through aa. they discuss the troubling history of addiction treatment—from asylums to the violent therapeutic community model created by synanon—and why compassionate, non-controlling approaches work better than punishment. evan challenges the disease model of addiction, arguing that addiction arises from disconnection, family systems, and a sick society. they also critique wilderness therapy and the troubled teen industry, and talk about what parents and teens can do when facing addiction: find community, take responsibility for family dynamics, and seek people who won't judge or control.
quote: addiction and mental health problems don't occur out of a vacuum. they occur out of a context.
quote_display: addiction and mental health problems don't occur out of a VACUUM. they occur out of a CONTEXT.
